disposition_reason: Baseline serum selenium in 12 338 French adults with lifestyle and dietary determinants.

study.design: cross-sectional baseline analysis of a national randomized supplementation trial cohort
study.market: volunteers recruited nationally after a media campaign
study.method: electrothermal atomic absorption spectrometry with Zeeman background correction and platinum modifier; standard addition calibration
study.qa: Seronorm serum internal quality control; interlaboratory comparison schemes

regulatory_or_exposure: Results: 1.3% of men and 1.7% of women below 0.75 umol/L (sub-deficiency cut-off cited from a European group)
Results: 25.3% of men and 17.4% of women above 1.25 umol/L, the value cited for optimal glutathione peroxidase activity
non_numeric_findings: Serum selenium rose with alcohol, meat and fish consumption and fell with smoking in both sexes (Abstract).
Obese women had lower serum selenium; in men, higher fruit and vegetable intake associated with lower serum selenium (Abstract).
Significant differences between French regions (Abstract; Fig. 1).
